title: feat(types)!: retire the `PartialSchema` export, which had no reader; a census pin keeps it gone (objectui#11608)
body:
Fixes #11608
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Retires the `PartialSchema` utility type (generic over a node type `T`) from `@object-ui/types`. It had no reader. The census ran at work time before any write; it found no reader in any repository it could read, so the seat's premised ruling (claim `5981086062`, executing triage `5979662969`) applies: retire, with no replacement alias.

## Census, run before the first edit

Hits are listed by file, never as a count. "Lit" means the control query returned a non-empty result in the same checkout, so a zero beside it is a reading.

| Repository | Read at | Searched | Hits | Control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| objectui | `b403bb36`, the branch base (`origin/main`) | `git grep -n -w PartialSchema` over every tracked file | The declaration and docblock in `packages/types/src/index.ts`. The import, and the "`PartialSchema` works as written" section, of `base-schema-closed-face-8347.test.ts`. Listed apart: the pending `.changeset/8347-baseschema-closed-face.md`, where one bullet describes the type, and `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md` (history). A case-insensitive substring query outside CHANGELOGs found nothing more. | `git grep -l -w SchemaByType`: lit |
| objectstack | `origin/main` `da40a5f6`, read through the owned ref `refs/os-dev/issue-11608/os-main` (no file edited) | `git grep -n -w PartialSchema`, then `git grep -n -i partialschema` | none | `git grep -l '@object-ui/types'`: lit |
| hotcrm | `4054ec26`, an anonymous shallow clone of `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` | `git grep -n -i partialschema` | none | `git grep -l '@object-ui/'`: lit. There is no `@object-ui/types` import to use as the control: hotcrm's metadata-reference test says the repo declares no `@object-ui/*` dependency. |
| cloud | n/a | **NOT MEASURED**: not reachable from this account | n/a | n/a |

The objectui hits are the declaration, its own docblock, the #8347 pin, and a pending note that describes the type. None of them reads it. With no reader anywhere the census reached, the ruling is retire. For any consumer the census could not see, cloud included, the changeset's migration is the answer.

## What this removes

- **`packages/types/src/index.ts`:** the `PartialSchema` export and its whole docblock. ⛔ No replacement alias. The sibling `SchemaByType` and everything else stay byte-identical.
- **`base-schema-closed-face-8347.test.ts`:** the `PartialSchema` rows. That is the import, section 4 ("`PartialSchema` works as written now"), and the two bindings that section fed into the vitest leg, whose length assertion moves with them. The `ButtonSchema` import goes too, because only section 4 read it. Sections 1 to 3 and the header are byte-identical, and the numbering stays coherent because section 4 was the last.
- ⛔ `.changeset/8347-baseschema-closed-face.md` is not edited (see the note under review notes).

## The census pin

`packages/types/src/__tests__/partial-schema-retired-11608.test.ts` reads the retirement through three instruments. Each one has a lit control.

1. **tsc** (`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, chained from the package's `type-check`) reads a `@ts-expect-error` row on the root barrel (`import('../index').PartialSchema`). Its control is the sibling `SchemaByType` through the same import form, with no directive.
2. **The `exports` map** (vitest) reads every entry's `types` target, maps it to the `src/` module that `tsc` emits it from, and asserts that each module exists and that none of them names `PartialSchema`. An entry added later is covered automatically. Control: the same read finds `export type SchemaByType` in the `.` entry's source. It reads `src/`, not `dist/`, because the per-PR `test` job builds nothing first.
3. **The tracked tree** (vitest) runs `git grep -nE` for the word over every tracked file except `*CHANGELOG.md`, `.changeset/` and the pin itself. A re-export chain is caught here: whatever module declares the alias names it, and that module is tracked. Control: the same probe finds `SchemaByType`.

The pin also compiles the changeset's TO spelling for `ButtonSchema`. It checks that the spelling keeps the same key set, that `type` stays required (a `@ts-expect-error` row), and that a misspelled key is refused (a `@ts-expect-error` row).

### Ablation (one-off proof, nothing left in the tree)

The fix was committed first (`de3dcf5b`). The mutation went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which puts `export type PartialSchema` back into `index.ts` right after `SchemaByType`. Its own on-disk evidence showed the anchor going from one hit to none, the replacement from none to one, and the blob changing. Both readings were taken on the mutated tree:

- **vitest:** the run went red, and the two absence tests failed by name. "no entry source module names `PartialSchema`" listed `. -> packages/types/src/index.ts`. "the symbol `PartialSchema` appears nowhere: ..." listed the restored `index.ts` declaration. Both lit controls and the TO-spelling leg stayed green.
- **tsc:** `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`, on the `_RetiredFromTheRootBarrel` row.
- **Restore:** `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path. The blob after the restore equals the HEAD blob (`333196a9`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty. After that, all of `packages/types` vitest and `type-check` went green at `de3dcf5b`.
- The first attempt was a no-op. The tool refused it because the replacement contained the anchor, so the anchor count did not drop. Nothing ran, and the file was restored. It was re-anchored and run again, and only that second run's reading is reported above.

## Changeset

`.changeset/11608-partialschema-retire.md`, `@object-ui/types: minor`. It carries a breaking banner, the line `**Clause-②: yes (narrowing)**`, and a FROM and TO pair:

- **FROM:** the `PartialSchema` import and annotation.
- **TO:** the node type's own declared members, or, for a partial value, `Partial` of `T` intersected with `{ type: T['type'] }`, written inline.

The TO spelling was checked to compile (generic and concrete) in a scratch program, with a control that went red. It is also pinned in the census pin above.

## Gates (local, at `de3dcf5b`)

- **`packages/types`:** `type-check` (all three `tsc` programs) green. vitest over `packages/types/` green. Both ran under `os-verify-lock`.
- **`pnpm lint` on the touched files:** eslint over the three touched `.ts` files is clean in its JSON output. This is a declared narrowing. The population is eslint's own config, and the file set is the three paths the JSON names. The invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- **The packages built for the dist-reading gates:** every package was built first (`pnpm --filter … run build`, no turbo cache touched). `dist/index.d.ts` names `SchemaByType` and not `PartialSchema`.
- **Green, with the built tree in place:** `pnpm check:readme-exports` and `pnpm check:doc-snippets`. `pnpm check:doc-types` is green too, although no doc names the type.
- **Also green:** `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (zero new citations) and `pnpm check:control-bytes`.
- **The changeset checkers:** `changeset:check` (fixed and no-major), `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-overwrite` (one added, nothing pre-existing modified), `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`. All green, and none objects to the two pending notes describing the same type.
- **Also run because the diff implicates them:** `type-check:coverage`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:component-surface-parity` (report-only) and `check:published-dist`. All exited 0.
- **The repo-wide `git grep -w PartialSchema` after the change**, outside CHANGELOGs, hits only the two pending changesets and the new pin. Its control, `SchemaByType`, is lit.

## Notes for review

- **Two pending notes about one type.** `.changeset/8347-baseschema-closed-face.md` has a bullet saying the alias "works as written". This PR removes the alias. Per the dispatch, the #8347 note is not edited here. This PR's changeset says that it supersedes that bullet. If both ship in the same release, the seat may want to drop or amend that bullet. No changeset checker objected.
- **Serial:** `origin/main` had not moved past `b403bb36` when this was opened, so merging it was a no-op. #11614 (which also touches `packages/types/src/index.ts`, in a disjoint region) was still open.
- No labels written; the dispatch named none.
